title: I was paid to write fake Google reviews – then my ‘bosses’ tried to scam me | Scams | The Guardian

facts.fact: A Telegram channel purporting to be Quad Marketing Agency had 16,800 subscribers, and a near-identical channel had 14,700 subscribers.
facts.quote: has 16,800 subscribers, while another near-identical channel has 14,700 subscribers

facts.fact: The fake-review scam channels offered up to 14 reviews per work session, initially paid at $5 per review.
facts.quote: up to 14 reviews, paid initially at $5 per review.

facts.fact: The scammer recruiter promised fake-review workers up to £800 a day, a claim the reporter chose to test.
facts.quote: the promises of up to £800 a day were true

facts.fact: Since 12 March, the scam channel had published nearly 6,000 posts asking for fake reviews.
facts.quote: Since 12 March, the channel had published nearly 6,000 posts asking for fake reviews.

facts.fact: The reporter received two or three offers of scam work a month because their number was on a list of potential targets.
facts.quote: so two or three offers of work come through a month

facts.fact: Telegram stated that its moderators remove millions of pieces of harmful content each day, including fraudulent review scams.
facts.quote: remove millions of pieces of harmful content each day

facts.fact: Booking.com said only customers with confirmed stays can post reviews on its platform.
facts.quote: only customers with confirmed stays were able to post reviews

facts.fact: Travelodge stated that under its customer review policy it does not create, commission or publish fake reviews under any circumstances.
facts.quote: we do not create, commission or publish fake reviews under any circumstances.

facts.fact: Under UK law, recipients of cryptocurrency payments must declare their source.
facts.quote: Under UK law recipients of cryptocurrency payments must declare their source.

facts.fact: USDC is a stablecoin pegged to the US dollar, which the scammers used for payments to workers.
facts.quote: USDC, a stablecoin that is pegged to the US dollar

facts.fact: The article states that customer-review fraud costs consumers billions of pounds a year in misdirected spending.
facts.quote: costing consumers billions of pounds a year in misdirected spending

facts.fact: Fraud consultant Serpil Hall has spent 20 years battling scammers.
facts.quote: a fraud consultant who has spent 20 years battling scammers

facts.fact: The UK Competition and Markets Authority found in 2023 that fake review text on products causes annual harm of between £50m and £312m to UK consumers.
facts.quote: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) in 2023 found that fake review text on products causes annual harm of

facts.fact: The CMA said it found 11% to 15% of all reviews were fake for the products it examined.
facts.quote: said it found 11% to 15% of all reviews were fake for the products it examined

facts.fact: The author received $5 per fake review paid in USDC.
facts.quote: I received $5 per fake review in USDC.

facts.fact: Wallets linked to the fake review payments tended to pay out between $300,000 and $600,000 in USDC before transferring the money on, according to Chainalysis's analysis.
facts.quote: The wallets tended to pay out between $300,000 and $600,000 in USDC before transferring the money on.

facts.fact: Under UK laws introduced in April 2025, web platforms such as Google carrying reviews must have clear policies on preventing and removing fake and incentivised reviews.
facts.quote: Under laws introduced in the UK last April, web platforms such as Google that carry reviews must have clear policies on the prevention and removal of fake and incentivised reviews

facts.fact: Google said it had removed more than 240m fake reviews since 2024, the vast majority before they were seen.
facts.quote: It said it had removed more than 240m fake reviews since 2024, the vast majority of which were removed before they were seen

facts.fact: Google said it restricted 900,000 accounts for violating policies.
facts.quote: and restricted 900,000 accounts for violating policies.

facts.fact: The scammers' 'business task' required paying $50 to receive $60 back.
facts.quote: which consisted of paying $50 and receiving $60 back.

facts.fact: A table shared by the scammers promised peak awards of $16,000 for an initial outlay of $10,000.
facts.quote: peaking at $16,000 for an initial outlay of $10,000.

facts.fact: The author made $30 from several hours of work spread over weeks.
facts.quote: I made $30 from several hours of work spread out over weeks.
